# Track 1 — the scoring runtime

*Generated by `usvnav docs` from usvnav 0.1.0. Do not edit; edit the code.*

What a submission meets at scoring time, identified as `usvnav-runtime/1` — the value the manifest's `runtime` field must carry.

| what | value |
|---|---|
| Python | 3.13 (major.minor pinned; the patch level is not) |
| `numpy` | 2.5.3, pinned exactly |
| `onnxruntime-gpu` | 1.23.2, pinned exactly |
| CUDA libraries | the pip packages onnxruntime-gpu loads, pinned exactly: `nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12==12.9.79`, `nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.25.1.1`, `nvidia-cublas-cu12==12.9.2.10`, `nvidia-cufft-cu12==11.4.1.4`, `nvidia-curand-cu12==10.3.10.19`, `nvidia-cuda-nvrtc-cu12==12.9.86`, `nvidia-nvjitlink-cu12==12.9.86` |
| execution providers | `CUDAExecutionProvider`, `CPUExecutionProvider` |
| other packages | the runtime's own packages — the standard library, numpy, onnxruntime and `usvnav` — may be imported; anything else your agent imports must be inside your submission directory, as pure Python or as wheels built for Linux x86_64 / CPython 3.13 (compiled extensions included) unpacked there |
| network | none |
| CPU | Intel Core i7-14700 (28 threads) |
| RAM | 30 GB |
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 (8 GB); onnxruntime's CUDAExecutionProvider is how a submission reaches it |
| sharing | the scoring PC may run several agents at the same time -- other episodes or other submissions -- sharing the CPU and the GPU; no CPU cores are pinned to an agent, and the time limits are wall clock under those conditions |
| memory limit | set by the scoring sandbox, not by the kit; see the problem page |
| time limits | 120 s of wall clock per episode, from the `reset(meta)` call to the end of the episode, the agent's time and the scorer's together (exceeded: that episode is `time_overrun`, and the agent's process is started again for the next episode); `Agent(config_path)` within 120 s |
| submission form | directory |
| agent process | a child of the runner, observation and action over a local pipe; one process per condition, constructed once, running that condition's episodes in sequence with reset() between them; a process that dies or overruns an episode is started again for the next one |
| wall clock | not real time -- the runner waits for act(); there is no per-tick limit, only the episode's |

The interpreter and the package set do not change during the contest. The shipped `usvnav` package depends on numpy and nothing else: everything the scorer runs has to exist on a machine with no network. How the runner applies the time limits is in `docs/RULES.md` §4. Contest rules — limits, scoring, ranking, what is published, the deadline — are on the site's problem page and common rules (https://kraftonai-autonomy-hackathon.com/problems/), which are authoritative.

## onnxruntime

The runtime provides `onnxruntime`, GPU build, so a learned component has one framework-neutral way to run: export to ONNX from PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX, ship the `.onnx` file inside your submission, and open it with `onnxruntime.InferenceSession(path, providers=["CUDAExecutionProvider", "CPUExecutionProvider"])`. It is the same version Track 3 pins, installed once on the scoring machine; nothing else about it is configured (default session options, no TensorRT). The CUDA provider is a pure win only for a model large enough to amortise the copy; a small network is often faster on the CPU provider, and the wall clock per tick counts against the time limits either way.

To match it locally — the interpreter and numpy too, not only onnxruntime: the kit installs on any Python from 3.10 and any numpy from 1.24, but the scorer runs Python 3.13 and numpy 2.5.3, and numpy 1.x and 2.x differ in type promotion and copy semantics, so develop on the scorer's versions:

```
python --version                        # 3.13.x, the scorer's interpreter
pip install numpy==2.5.3
pip install onnxruntime-gpu==1.23.2 nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12==12.9.79 nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.25.1.1 nvidia-cublas-cu12==12.9.2.10 nvidia-cufft-cu12==11.4.1.4 nvidia-curand-cu12==10.3.10.19 nvidia-cuda-nvrtc-cu12==12.9.86 nvidia-nvjitlink-cu12==12.9.86
pip install onnxruntime==1.23.2          # CPU build: same API, same numbers to float precision, no card needed
```

The GPU build finds its CUDA libraries in those pip packages; no system CUDA install is needed or used.
